narrative:
The FY2026 Rare Disease plan targets USD 8.35B net sales across 5 therapy areas, 10 brand-indications and 5 markets — +8.3% over the FY2025 actual of USD 7.71B, and 1.8% below the CFO envelope of USD 8.5B.

Ultomiris is the engine: USD 5.03B across PNH, gMG, NMOSD and aHUS, with Neurology now the largest therapy area at USD 2.55B. Strensiq HPP adds USD 1.35B; Soliris declines to USD 1.02B as patients convert and eculizumab biosimilars enter Europe and the US.

This is the planning model that runs in a standalone Anaplan instance today. Here it runs on the same governed actuals as the finance semantic layer — targets cascade in real time and write back to a hybrid table, with no extract and no reconciliation step.

signals.title: Rare Disease FY2026 Planning Guidance
signals.excerpt: FY2026 rare disease net sales envelope set at USD 8.5B. Planning to move from the standalone Anaplan model onto the finance semantic layer on Snowflake.

signals.title: Planning Platform Containment Memo
signals.excerpt: Containment mode: no net-new finance platforms. Rare disease planning pilot runs on existing Snowflake actuals and retires one standalone planning platform.

signals.title: gMG Claims Analysis — Diagnosis-to-Treatment Time
signals.excerpt: Median time from gMG diagnosis to complement inhibitor start fell from 14 to 9 months. AChR+ antibody testing up 22% YoY.
